liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancin' in the Streets** (5 reviews): Very far-out version that gets spacey toward its close; Leads into what the reviewer calls the best Drums/Space they've heard [16][17][18][19][23]
- **Tennessee Jed** (2 reviews): Reviewer thinks this Tennessee Jed may be the strongest ever played; Named as a first-set high point [15][24]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (2 reviews): Lazy Lightnin' into Supplication gave the first set a sign of the band gathering momentum; Lazy Lightnin' into Supplication cited as a first-set highlight [21][24]
- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): Jerry and Bob both strum energetically, and they sound like they're enjoying themselves; Reviewer calls it fantastic, with spirit evident in Jerry's singing [16][22]
- **Black Peter** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out this Black Peter as a favorite; Second-set Black Peter singled out as especially good [19][24]
- **Mississippi Half Step** (1 review): Defends it as a nice version that builds momentum into Franklin's Tower, rejecting a claim it was a joke [22]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Very energetic, with Donna belting out her vocals [17]

## The recordings

- **gd78-10-20.sbd.lai.4159.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 163 min; rated 4.36/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has noticeable hiss; Sound quality is good but not outstanding [15][18]
- **gd1978-10-20.sbd.nugs.21245.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 163 min [3]. Said about its sound: Has minor flaws, including cuts caused by cassette changes [3]
- **gd1978-10-20.166111.aud.remaster.acetboy.flac1644**: audience recording; 20 songs; 161 min [4]
- **gd1978-10-20.sbd.miller.92542.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 167 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [7]. Said about its sound: Charlie Miller soundboard that the reviewer finds great sounding [23]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls a vivid psychedelic experience of the stage pulling downward, needing to keep dancing, and forgetting later songs [20]
- Reviewer says several other 1978 shows are better than this one [15]
- Part of the Winterland 'From Egypt with Love' run; reviewer feels this show gets overlooked among them [16]
- Reviewer ranks October 18 above this show, with better sound; both have strong sets [19]
- Reviewer saw the run: Tuesday was outstanding, Wednesday built slowly to a blaze, and this Friday opened only okay [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd78-10-20.sbd.lai.4159.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard transferred and seeded to etree by Mike Lai, from a Bruce Fried DAT [1]
- **gd1978-10-20.sbd.nugs.21245.sbeok.flac16**: source: SBD>Master Reel>Cassette>DAT>WAV [3]. Also: Compilation of soundboards for all five October 1978 Winterland shows, with varying quality and some spliced sources [3]
- **gd1978-10-20.166111.aud.remaster.acetboy.flac1644**: taped by Reinhart Hohlwein; transferred by acetboy; source: 2 x AKG D224e => Sony TC-158 >> MAC [4]. Also: Remaster of an earlier shn audience-source transfer, number 100700; Small soundboard patches in Franklin's Tower and Not Fade Away were smoothed and disguised; Remastered in ocenaudio and Harrison Mixbus, mainly balancing RMS levels across channels and frequencies [4]
- **gd1978-10-20.sbd.miller.92542.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Maxell UDXL-I) -> PCM (Analog Out) -> DSony R500 (A>D Only) -> Peak -> AIFF D [7]
